correctness.rationale: Ultrahomogeneity classifies types by an admissible downset and upset over the named vertices; when both are nonempty, every cross-pair must be present. Ideals are encoded by an omitted subset of A and an included subset of B whose cross-pairs are all missing. This gives the finite formulas, including isolated points and p=0,1. The mixed missing-edge contribution to J_n has mean at most q_n^(-1)((1+q_n)^n−1)^2=o(2^n). For W_{n,k}, the factor (1+p_n^k)^n/2^n is asymptotic to n^(−k)exp(−kt/2). For overlap r>0, a column contributes 1+2p_n^k+p_n^(2k−r); relative to the product mean this gives exp(n r q_n/4+O_k(n q_n²))=O(n^(r/2)), and O(n^(2k−r)) pairs yield a normalized variance O(n^(−1/2)); disjoint sets have zero covariance. For the tail, after halving by shore symmetry, for i≤n^(3/5) the normalized summand is at most (C_t/i)^i since n q_n² i=o(1); for n^(3/5)<i≤n/log n, the combinatorial log cost −i log i wins over (1/2+o(1))i log n. In the next range H(.1)≈.325<log(2/(1+e^(−2)))≈.566. If both shores exceed n/10, the exponential edge penalty beats 4^n. Thus the normalized expected double-large tail vanishes as K→∞. Finite-k opposite-orientation overlap is polynomially bounded, so ties have vanishing probability; individual fringe masses converge and their tails are tight. Since M_n/2^n tends to a positive constant for every fixed finite t, the conditional TV distance converges to zero in probability (not an almost-sure claim).
